attorneys.name: Sarah L. Newell
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Wichita, KS
attorneys.bio:
Sarah L. Newell has been in private practice, practicing bankruptcy law since 2002. She is admitted to the Kansas and Missouri State Bars. She represents both debtors and creditors. Prior to private practice, she clerked for Judge John K. Pearson and Judge Robert E. Nugent.

She earned her Bachelor's degree in 1996 and her Juris Doctorate in 1998, both from the University of Kansas.

She currently practices in the areas of bankruptcy, collections and family law. She resides in Wichita with her husband and three children.

Filing for Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy is not an easy decision to make. Every situation, like every client, is different and requires representation tailored to their unique needs and circumstances. At Gibson Watson Marino LLC, our attorney, Sarah Newell, hones in on your individual needs to derive the best possible way forward for your case.

Bankruptcy should be viewed as a financial planning tool to help you find your way towards a brighter financial future. Whether you are facing a foreclosure, garnishments, judgments, or other collection activity, you owe it to yourself to learn more about options available to you.

attorneys.name: Eli O'Brien
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Wichita, KS
attorneys.bio:
Mr. O'Brien grew up in the small rural Kansas community of Osage City, graduating from Osage City High School in 2004. From there, he attended classes at Butler Community College for two years while serving as a videographer for the Butler Grizzlies' nationally renowned football program.

After Butler, Mr. O'Brien transferred to Emporia State University where he majored in History, a discipline that honed the research skills necessary to serve his ultimate goal of being a criminal defense attorney. Mr. O'Brien graduated in 2009 and went to work in the private sector for two years before entering Washburn University School of Law in 2011. While at Washburn, he took several courses focusing on the practice of criminal law and competed as a member of one of Washburn's trial teams in his third year of law school.

After graduation, Mr. O'Brien went to work for the Sedgwick County Public Defender's office where he provided legal advice and trial counsel to indigent people accused of serious felony offenses. While there, he acquired impressive jury trial experience in cases accusing murder, aggravated assault, and rape. His jury trials have resulted in a number of acquittals.

His practice at Monnat & Spurrier, Chartered, focuses on the defense of serious felony accusations. O'Brien is a 2019 graduate of the National Criminal Defense College Trial Practice Institute, Roger Williams School of Law, Bristol, Rhode Island, and has been named to the list of Best Lawyers in America each year since 2021.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Mr. O'Brien grew up in the small rural Kansas community of Osage City, graduating from Osage City High School in 2004. From there, he attended classes at Butler Community College for two years while serving as a videographer for the Butler Grizzlies' nationally renowned football program.

After Butler, Mr. O'Brien transferred to Emporia State University where he majored in History, a discipline that honed the research skills necessary to serve his ultimate goal of being a criminal defense attorney. Mr. O'Brien graduated in 2009 and went to work in the private sector for two years before entering Washburn University School of Law in 2011. While at Washburn, he took several courses focusing on the practice of criminal law and competed as a member of one of Washburn's trial teams in his third year of law school.

After graduation, Mr. O'Brien went to work for the Sedgwick County Public Defender's office where he provided legal advice and trial counsel to indigent people accused of serious felony offenses. While there, he acquired impressive jury trial experience in cases accusing murder, aggravated assault, and rape. His jury trials have resulted in a number of acquittals.

His practice at Monnat & Spurrier, Chartered, focuses on the defense of serious felony accusations. O'Brien is a 2019 graduate of the National Criminal Defense College Trial Practice Institute, Roger Williams School of Law, Bristol, Rhode Island, and has been named to the list of Best Lawyers in America each year since 2021.

attorneys.name: Braden M. Perry
attorneys.practice_type: Government Investigations/White-Collar Defense Lawyers in Mission Woods, KS
attorneys.bio:
Braden Perry is a former federal enforcement attorney and veteran in regulatory compliance and white-collar defense, Mr. Perry has the expertise and consults with clients throughout the United States in areas of internal investigations, enforcement matters, regulatory issues, and corporate transactions, including advising on highly complex regulatory structures. Mr. Perry routinely guides clients through all stages of litigation and specializes in complex, high-stakes disputes involving matters of first impression. He also serves as an expert witness in complex financial matters. This litigation experience is vital when advising clients in multifaceted criminal and regulatory issues. Mr. Perry also has a deep understanding of the vast array of statutes, regulations, caselaw, and other requirements involved in civil forfeiture.

Before forming Kennyhertz Perry, Mr. Perry was a Chief Compliance Officer/Chief Regulatory Attorney of a global financial services and FINRA member firm. He handled all aspects of compliance and regulatory responsibilities for multiple registered investment advisors, mutual funds, alternative investments, and a broker-dealer. Mr. Perry focused on identifying and assessing the compliance risks of the firms, creating and implementing policies and procedures that address and allow compliance risks to be managed, and reviewing the policies and procedures to determine their continued adequacy and effectiveness.

Previously, Mr. Perry served as a senior trial attorney for CFTC, managing a team of trial attorneys, investigators and support staff in the investigation and prosecution of market manipulation, market abuse, and fraud in the futures and derivatives markets, advising staff in areas of investigations, leading investigations of high profile matters, and facilitating effective engagement and collaborative work with other U.S. regulatory and prosecutorial bodies, international regulators, and exchange staff. Mr. Perry served as a liaison to the Office of General Counsel in the revision of CFTC policies and procedures under regulatory reform, including Dodd-Frank, including drafting provisions for the enforcement of complex derivative swaps. He was also named to a CFTC, SEC, and FERC interagency task force on the federal collection and retention of sensitive data.

Mr. Perry began his career in the Blackwell Sanders Government Compliance, Investigations, and Litigation, White-Collar Criminal Defense, Commercial and Business Litigation, and Digital Discovery and Records Management practice groups. He represented clients in the prosecution and defense of complex business disputes in domestic and international jurisdictions, served as counsel to publicly and privately held companies undergoing both internal and external investigations, assisted clients in recognizing and avoiding the expanding risk of corporate criminal liability, and designing and implementing targeted corporate compliance programs. Mr. Perry was a founding member of the electronic discovery practice group and has first-chaired trials in Missouri Circuit Courts and Kansas Chapter 60 and 61 courts, representing both plaintiffs and defendants in various financial, commercial, criminal, and collection matters.

Mr. Perry is a graduate of the University of Kansas School of Law and Kansas State University. During his time in law school, Mr. Perry was a member of the Kansas Journal of Law & Public Policy. Mr. Perry is admitted to practice law in Kansas and Missouri and has held the Series 7, 24, and 66 licenses with FINRA. Mr. Perry also serves as a National Futures Association and FINRA arbitrator. He regularly conducts various regulatory training with clients and is a frequent speaker on emerging legal topics. Mr. Perry is a regular contributor and media source appearing in over 150 financial and legal publications.

attorneys.name: Justen Phelps
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Defense Lawyers in Wichita, KS
attorneys.bio:
Justen Phelps’s practice focuses primarily on medical malpractice defense, insurance defense, and general civil litigation matters touching on a wide variety of areas including consumer protection claims, contractual disputes, corporate ownership and operation, real estate and construction. He is an experienced litigator with extensive courtroom experience handling complex legal matters. As a full-time prosecutor, prior to joining Gibson Watson Marino, LLC, Justen tried more than 50 felony jury trials and argued before the Kansas Court of Appeals. Over more than a decade since joining the firm, he has applied his litigation experience and training to challenging civil matters on behalf of his clients including multiple successful jury trials and appeals.

Justen grew up in Wichita, KS, and attended college at the University of Kansas where he received a B.A. in History. He then attended law school at Ave Maria School of Law where he graduated with honors in 2006.

Justen is admitted to practice before the Supreme Court of Kansas, the Supreme Court of Missouri, the United States District Court for Kansas, and the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals. He has also appeared in courts throughout the country, including California, Illinois, Washington and Delaware. Justen serves as the City Prosecutor for the City of Rose Hill and the City of Augusta. He has served as the Chair of the Wichita Bar Association’s Civil Practice Committee.

attorneys.name: John L. Richeson
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Ottawa, KS
attorneys.bio:
John has been with Anderson & Byrd in private practice since his graduation from the University of Kansas School of Law in 1965. He served as City Attorney for the City of Ottawa, Kansas for 27 years. John has also served as attorney for several other cities, unified school districts, a university, special counsel to several Boards of County Commissioners, Rural Water Districts, Kansas Board of Pharmacy, commercial banks, agricultural lenders and many charitable and religious organizations. He has been involved in representation of many clients appearing before administrative and quasi-governmental bodies for motor carriers, applicants, protestants, landowners, oil and gas producers, taxpayers, licensees and citizens.

John has spent over 57 years practicing in oil and gas, estate planning, real property including examination of title to land and titles to oil and gas properties, contracts, eminent domain and general practice. He assists other members of the firm with creative ideas, research and writing. He believes the law firm works for a client as a team by comparison of ideas and approaches which best fit and suit the client.

John is a founding board member of the Franklin County Community Foundation which administers several million dollars in endowments established through donor directed trusts which fund local community needs educationally, benevolently, charitably and religiously.

He is a member of the American Bar Association, a life time member of the Kansas Bar Association and the Franklin County Bar Association. He served as President of the Kansas Bar Association Administrative Law Section. John is a Fellow of the Kansas Bar Foundation. He is admitted to practice in all Kansas state and federal Courts, U.S. Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals and the U.S. Supreme Court. Also, John was formerly a Kansas Supreme Court Approved Mediator. Further, he has served as an investigator for the Office of Disciplinary Administrator for more than 40 years.

John has appeared as counsel of record in litigation filed in more than half of the 105 courthouses in Kansas. He has appeared in numerous appeals in the Kansas Court of Appeals, the Kansas Supreme Court and the U.S. Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals.

John and his wife, Jan are the parents of two children. They are grandparents to nine grandchildren. John and Jan enjoy their leisure time together.

attorneys.name: Richard G. Rozier Ph.D.
attorneys.practice_type: Patent Application Preparation and Prosecution Lawyers in Overland Park, KS
attorneys.bio:
Richard received a PhD in Electrical Engineering from UNC Charlotte in 1998. While in graduate school, he authored over a dozen conference or journal papers and presented papers at several conferences. After graduation, he worked as a Member of Technical Staff at Bell Labs in Holmdel, NJ doing research and development in integrated circuit design for use in optical communications with the Optical Data Networks group. During his tenure at Bell Labs, he was an inventor on two U.S. patents. In 2000, he left Bell Labs to join Xanoptix, Inc., a startup company in Merrimack, NH that manufactured optical transceiver cores, where he worked as a test and development engineer.

In 2006, Richard joined Hovey Williams LLP to become a patent agent. He has focused his practice as a patent agent on the preparation and prosecution of patent applications in the broad areas of mechanical components, electronics, signal processing, computer systems, software, and communications systems. Specifically, he has experience preparing and prosecuting patent applications involving electric motor assemblies and control circuitry, optical fiber components, laser amplifier systems, smartphone and other handheld devices hardware and applications, fitness band and smartwatch devices, integrated circuit and printed circuit board design, integrated circuit wafer fabrication systems, wireless communication electronic circuitry, advanced manufacturing systems including 3D printing, composite material component manufacturing, aviation navigation and radar systems, personal and automobile navigation systems, marine sonar systems, machine learning software, big data analysis software, and audio electronics, among others.

attorneys.name: Ron Rundberg
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Overland Park, KS
attorneys.bio:
Ron Rundberg is the founder of Rundberg Law, LLC. Previously, Ron was a shareholder in the law firm of Ferree, Bunn, Rundberg & Ridgway, Chartered from 1998 to 2018. From 1991 to 1997, Ron was an associate attorney with the firm. He obtained his law degree from the University Of Kansas School Of Law in 1991. In 1980, Ron graduated from Mid-America Nazarene College with a B.A., cum laude, in Business Administration. He is licensed to practice law in the states of Kansas and Missouri, U.S. District Courts for the District of Kansas and Western District of Missouri, as well as in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit. Mr. Rundberg has been a speaker on topics related to divorce, the impact of divorce on business, and adoption.

Since 2014, judges and other attorneys have designated Mr. Rundberg to be AV Preeminent™ Peer Review Rated by Martindale-Hubbell®. This means that he has been recognized for having the “highest level of professional excellence” for both legal ability and ethical standards. Since 2016, he has also been selected to Missouri and Kansas Super Lawyers. Only 5% of attorneys in Missouri and Kansas receive this distinction. He also has an Avvo rating of 10, Superb.

Mr. Rundberg understands this is probably the most difficult time of your life. You need an attorney who will work with you to effectively deal with the issues that are important to you. Too many attorneys make the resolution of cases more difficult and expensive than is necessary. Ron will always use an approach to maximize the result for you and minimize the expense. If the opposing party is unreasonable, Mr. Rundberg has extensive experience in representing clients in the courtroom.

Prior to graduating from law school, Mr. Rundberg was the co-founder of an adoption agency and the general manager of a family-owned manufacturing company. Ron has personal experience in dealing with the impact of divorce. Mr. Rundberg lives with his wife in Olathe, Kansas. They have a blended family of five adult children. He is active in community and church activities.

attorneys.name: R. Scott Ryburn
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Ottawa, KS
attorneys.bio:
Scott has been engaged in the practice of law in Franklin County, Kansas, since graduating from Washburn University School of Law in 1985. He began as an associate with the firm, and then spent two years as an Assistant County Attorney in 1993-1994. Since his return to the firm in 1995, Scott has concentrated his practice in areas of personal injury, wrongful death, oil and gas, insurance law, municipal law, real estate, banking, probate and commercial litigation.

He is admitted to practice before all courts in Kansas, including the U.S. District Court for the District of Kansas. He was also admitted to the United States Supreme Court in 2004. In 1996, Scott was appointed as a magistrate pro-tem and continues to serve in that capacity for the Fourth Judicial District of Kansas. He also served three consecutive terms on the Fourth Judicial District Nominating Committee which nominates District Judges.

Scott has tried cases in all areas of civil and criminal law, the Kansas Court of Appeals, focusing on representing plaintiffs in personal injury, wrongful death and oil and gas. Scott has tried numerous jury trials as well as argued several cases before the Kansas Court of Appeals.

attorneys.practice_type: Wills, Trusts and Probate Lawyers in Ottawa, KS
attorneys.bio:
Tom received a B.A. from the University of Kansas in 1971, and his Juris Doctor degree from the University School of Law in 1974.

He began the private practice of law in Franklin County in 1974, engaging in a general trial practice for 17 years as a partner with Green & Sachse, Chtd.

In 1991, Tom was appointed to the position of District Judge for the Fourth Judicial District of Kansas, and served there for 23 years. During his tenure on the bench, he was assigned to the domestic, criminal and probate divisions.

In 2014, Tom resumed the practice of law with the firm of Anderson & Byrd, LLP. There, he provides a variety of services to the firm's clients, primarily in the areas of wills and trusts, family law and mediation. He is also a Kansas Supreme Court approved mediator for core, domestic and civil areas of dispute.

Tom is a member of the Kansas Bar Association and past president of the Franklin County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Erica K. Schoenig J.D.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Olathe, KS
attorneys.bio:
Erica Schoenig is an experienced trial lawyer who aggressively represents clients who have been accused of criminal matters such as drug possession, drug sales, manufacture of drugs, domestic violence, DUI, crimes of violence, sex crimes, firearms charges, felony cases, misdemeanor crimes, all traffic tickets, minor in possession of alcohol, juvenile crimes, and probation and diversion violations. In an era where laws are increasingly restricting individual liberties, Erica puts her experience to work for her clients as she fights to protect their constitutional rights. As a former prosecutor, Erica knows her way around the courtroom as she has prepared hundreds of cases for trial and has a high success rate for the cases she has taken to jury trial both as a prosecutor and defense attorney. Whether a client has been charged with a serious felony crime or traffic ticket, Erica is known for her meticulous attention to detail and determination to achieve case resolutions that satisfy her clients.

Erica's first job after law school was working as a law clerk for judges in Johnson County, Kansas. That position allowed her to apply and further develop her legal research and writing skills as she worked closely with judges in the courthouse. Erica next accepted a position as a prosecuting attorney in the Johnson County, Kansas District Attorney's Office. She prosecuted cases for over six years, gaining in-depth experience as a trial lawyer. Erica prosecuted serious crimes such as murder cases and sex crimes, was a member of the office drug unit, which focused on prosecutions of high-level drug crimes for four years, and also prosecuted domestic violence crimes exclusively for thirteen months.

In April 2007, Erica began her career working as a defense attorney and fighting for individuals who have been accused of crimes. Her experiences as a law clerk and prosecutor help her to be a stronger advocate for her clients inside and outside the courtroom. Erica's high level of professionalism is an asset to clients when she obtains plea offers for them. When it comes to plea offers for clients Erica's motto is simple: the plea offer needs to be fair and reasonable. Some cases just need to be taken to trial. For clients wanting trials, Erica works closely with the client as a trial strategy is developed. Prosecutors have commented to Erica that it seems she knows the case better than the prosecutor by the time it gets to trial.

Erica began developing her courtroom and trial skills long before she went to law school. She has extensive music performance experience. In 1998, she graduated with honors from Wichita State University with degrees in music performance and music education and has performed in front of crowds for most of her life. While at Wichita State, Erica was one of a select group of musicians chosen in a contest to perform a solo selection with a symphony orchestra. Erica's leadership skills as an attorney were developed at Wichita State, as well. As a member of her sorority, Delta Delta Delta, Erica held officer positions, including President, and also received a national leadership award. She was also awarded the prestigious recognition of being chosen as a Senior Honor Woman at Wichita State University. Erica graduated from the University of Kansas School of Law in 2001. While in law school, Erica focused on gaining practical experience for her future criminal law career by serving as an intern for the United States Attorney's Office and the Johnson County District Attorney's Office. She also spent a school year working with the Defender Project at KU investigating and writing appeals for clients convicted of state and federal crimes.

Erica is a member of the Kansas Bar Association, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Kansas Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the Johnson County Bar Association. As a companion part of her practice to criminal defense of individuals in domestic violence cases, Erica also represents victims in domestic violence cases. Whether a victim is facing potential criminal charges, or needs help requesting modification of no contact orders in front of a judge, Erica has extensive experience dealing with those issues in court. In addition to criminal law matters, Erica also handles family law cases such as divorce, paternity, child custody, child support, protection from abuse and stalking orders.

Erica grew up on her family's farm in Western Kansas. Erica's strong work ethic was developed as she helped her family with the farm work during her growing years. Erica and her husband, Brian, are the proud parents of their most important treasures, their two daughters.

attorneys.name: Samel "Devin" Seward Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Wichita, KS
attorneys.bio:
Facing a divorce in Wichita, Kansas is a complicated process. Throughout your case, it is common to feel overwhelmed and stressed by the situation. Having dedicated and compassionate legal representation in your corner can provide you with peace of mind and educated guidance throughout the legal process. Samuel “Devin” Seward is an Associate Attorney with Stange Law Firm. From the firm’s Wichita, Kansas family law office, he can represent individuals throughout Sedgwick County and the surrounding communities.

Devin attended law school at Washburn University School of Law in Topeka, Kansas, where he earned his Juris Doctorate in May 2011. While in law school, Devin also served as a member of the Phi Alpha Delta law fraternity. Before law school, he earned his Bachelor of Arts in Accounting from Southwestern College in Winfield, Kansas in May 2007. Devin is licensed to practice law in the state of Kansas.

Before joining the Wichita, Kansas divorce and family lawyers at Stange Law Firm, Devin most recently served as Assistant City Attorney and City Prosecutor for the City of Newton, Kansas, where he advised on a range of municipal legal matters, conducted legal research, and prosecuted criminal, traffic, and code violation cases through plea negotiations, diversion agreements, or trial. Before that, he worked as an associate attorney focused on estate planning, preparing legal documents such as wills, trusts, and powers of attorney, and tailoring strategies to meet client objectives. In an earlier associate role, he handled civil litigation and contract matters, including drafting leases and real estate agreements, while also serving as court-appointed counsel in criminal defense cases involving charges like DUI and narcotics possession. Devin also brings nearly a decade of experience as an in-house landman for BEREXCO LLC, where he negotiated oil and gas lease renewals and ensured accuracy in lease data and financial reconciliation.

Note: The choice of a lawyer is an important decision and should not be based solely upon advertisements.

attorneys.name: Daniel L. Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Overland Park, KS
attorneys.bio:
Daniel L. Smith is a principal partner of Ankerholz and Smith in Overland Park, Kansas where he has practiced for more than 30 years since beginning the practice of law in 1976. Mr. Smith is a sixth generation Kansan and grew up in the east central Kansas town of Pleasanton where his father operated a family pharmacy. His experience working in the family business gave him an early interest and understanding of many medical issues and conditions. He attended the University of Kansas where he received his college undergraduate education. He is a graduate of Duke University School of Law.

Mr. Smith practices in the area of civil litigation, with an emphasis on injury cases arising both at work and elsewhere. He is interested in medical issues as well as significant engineering matters. He has participated in several advancements in Kansas law, including the adoption of the Dual Capacity Doctrine which permits an action between an employee and employer for negligence under certain special circumstances. He has been selected for inclusion in Who's Who in American Law since 2000.

Living a few miles from the Mine Creek Civil War Battlefield in his youth, Mr. Smith developed an early interest in history and historic preservation. He continues to be active in advocating for various historic preservation issues in Kansas and Missouri. He has been active in other civic, business and school organizations in his community.

Mr. Smith's wife, Alana, is a former professor at Kansas State University in the Speech and English Departments. They are the parents of three daughters.

attorneys.name: Laura Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Prairie Village, KS
attorneys.bio:
After earning her bachelor’s degree in Environmental Studies from the University of Kansas in 1999, Laura Smith remained at the University of Kansas School of Law and obtained her Juris Doctorate. After passing the Kansas (2002) and Missouri (2003) bars, Laura worked in a variety of legal areas, including trusts, estate planning, business formation, insurance claims, landlord/tenant matters, and criminal defense.

In 2007, Laura became an Assistant District Attorney, first in Wyandotte County, Kansas before then moving to the Johnson County District Attorney’s in 2008. Laura spent 7.5 years prosecuting high-level drug cases, including the manufacture, cultivation, and distribution of narcotics, and her final year focused on charging cases for the Johnson County District Attorney’s Office. These experiences gave her a broad base of knowledge. During her career in prosecution, she was able to handle a number of high-level and high-profile cases, including person, property, and drug crimes.

After 10 years in prosecution, Laura began her practice in family law in 2016. Her family law practice includes divorce, paternity, modification, child custody, child support, protection orders, and guardianships. Working in family law has been extremely fulfilling and has allowed Laura to continue her passion for helping others during some of their most challenging life experiences. “Divorce can be extremely stressful. It can be extremely consuming for people,” Smith said, “Your whole life is up in the air, but that’s where having the right attorney, the right partner in this process, makes all the difference.”

attorneys.name: Paul Snyder
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial and Business Litigation Lawyers in Overland Park, KS
attorneys.bio:
Paul has practiced for more than 30 years as a litigator. A main area of practice is representing investors in mortgage-backed securities (MBS) and similar financial litigation. In addition to complex commercial litigation, Paul has experience in financial and consumer class actions, title insurance and escrow litigation, and general breach of contract and breach of warranty claims.

Paul has recently expanded his practice to probate administration/litigation, and employment law, representing both employees and employers in all aspects of the employment relationship, from hiring to termination.

Regarding his MBS experience, Paul successfully tried back-to-back jury cases against Bank of America in Ohio (see news release) and Oklahoma (see news release) where unanimous juries found that LaSalle Bank (which was acquired by Bank of America), breached numerous representations and warranties in originating and securitizing four separate commercial loans. These cases are believed to be the first two CMBS repurchase cases ever to be tried to a jury. Paul's CMBS work was featured in an article in the Kansas City Business Journal (see article).

Comprehensive and voluminous discovery conducted by Paul in the individual repurchase lawsuits revealed numerous underlying systemic flaws in the LaSalle Bank loan program, which ultimately led to the filing of a global repurchase lawsuit against Bank of America (see news release). This federal court lawsuit sought the repurchase of approximately 750 multifamily loans - nearly all of the loans that LaSalle Bank securitized in two CMBS pools - each pool originally containing nearly half a billion dollars in commercial multifamily loans.

Prior to establishing the Snyder Law Firm in 2007, Paul worked at two of the largest law firms in Kansas City: Shook, Hardy & Bacon and Polsinelli, where he handled complex commercial litigation for clients on a national basis, as well as title insurance and escrow, breach of contract and other commercial disputes, fraud claims and employment non-compete claims in state and federal courts across the country. Paul also has extensive products liability experience, serving as both national and local counsel for numerous manufacturers, pharmaceutical companies and product suppliers.

Before joining the private practice of law, Paul was a criminal prosecutor for two years in Johnson County, Kansas. Paul graduated from the University of Kansas School of Law, where he was Note and Comment Editor of the University of Kansas Law Review, and member of the National Moot Court Team. He holds a B.S. in Journalism from the University of Kansas. Prior to law school Paul was a television reporter for the NBC affiliate in Wichita, Kansas for five years.

attorneys.name: John R. Stanley
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation representing Claimants only Lawyers in Overland Park, KS
attorneys.bio:
I am a Missouri and Kansas workers compensation lawyer and a member of the Missouri Bar Association, the Kansas Bar Association, the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association, and the Missouri Association of Trial Lawyers. Check me out at the Missouri Bar Lawyer Directory and/or the Kansas Bar Lawyer Directory.

I graduated in May 1980 from Washburn Law School in Topeka, Kansas. I took the Kansas bar exam in August 1980 and became licensed to practice law in Kansas in September 1980. I became licensed in Missouri in 1995. With the exception of two years when I worked as a lawyer in State and Federal government, I have been in private practice. I moved back to my home town in Syracuse Kansas and had a general small town law practice for 8 years. In 1990 I moved to the Kansas City area. Since 1992 I have been in private practice concentrating almost exclusively in workers compensation. In 1994 I obtained a Missouri law license and widened my practice to include injured workers in the State of Missouri, also. . I have been around the block a few times.

I have continuously practiced law for more than 27 years. And for the past 13 years my practice has been devoted exclusively to injured workers.

I must admit that my first experience with workers compensation was working in a firm that worked for employers and insurance companies about 95% of the time. I lasted about a year. That was in 1992-1993. I hated it. Honestly I didn't sleep well at night. I realized that my job was to save my client, employers and insurance companies, money. I dealt with many workers who did not have lawyers and who did not know their rights. They thought they were saving themselves money by not hiring an attorney. I dealt with many workers who had lawyers who were inexperienced in the area of workers compensation. I did my job, but my heart was not in it. After a year I left that firm and have devoted myself since to the rights of the injured worker. I have not represented an insurance company since I left that firm in 1993. I must say that my pillow is much softer now.

I was born and raised in a small town of less than 2000 in western Kansas. I was the 6th of 7 children. It was a great place to grow up and I learned old-fashioned family values from my father. - who owned a small business. He never had the opportunity to go to the college, but worked hard to give me that opportunity. In the summer months I worked long hours on the farm and learned to work hard.

I attended community college and graduated from the University of Kansas with a degree in economics in 1976. I worked and saved money for a year and then entered law school and graduated three years later in 1980.

I met and married the love of my life in 1978. Connie and I have been married more than 29 years now. We have four children who we are very proud of two boys and two girls, David, Sarah, Amanda and Andrew. They have all left the nest. David and his wife Kristan have blessed us with two grandchildren, Lauren and Benjamin while Amanda and her husband Mike also have a daughter Katelyn.

My first 8 years of practicing law were in my home town of Syracuse. There I represented one of the two town banks, the School District, numerous farmers and ranchers, merchants, cowboys (and cowgirls), truckers, feedlot workers, mechanics. I represented those charged with crimes from speeding to larceny to rape. After two years I was elected County Attorney and then prosecuted crimes from D.U.I.'s, thefts, rapes and one murder case. It was a great experience. My children walked to school. I walked three blocks to my office. It was not uncommon for to greet the bank president and the town drunk (both on first name basis) on the two block walk to the post office.

Over the years much of my family and friends had moved to the Kansas City area. My wife is from Kansas City, Missouri and it was only natural that I was lured to the "big city". It too has been a wonderful experience both for my family and myself.

In western Kansas I barely knew what workers compensation was. In Kansas (and Missouri for that matter) farmers are not required to have workers compensation insurance. There was a meat packing plant in Garden City 50 miles away, but those cases were handled by local attorneys. In 8 years I had one small workers compensation case. After plowing through the books and the procedures I was able to get my client a settlement. It was a simple case and not a very serious injury. It was a tremendous amount of work for a small fee. "That will be the last work comp case for me", I thought.

After a short stint as an attorney handling banking and real estate law (which I considered pretty boring) I hooked up with a law school friend who talked me into joining his firm - a workers compensation defense firm. Although I did my job and saved my insurance clients lots of money - at the expense of injured workers, I did not like myself. I was miserable. Now that I am representing injured workers exclusively, I sleep much better. In fact I have been able to use what I learned "on the other side" in order to better represent my injured worker clients.

Although my practice concentrates only on workers compensation I have represented the whole gambit of injured workers: assembly line workers, boiler makers, steel workers, truck drivers, nurses, secretaries, waitresses, construction workers, even insurance adjusters! And the list goes on. I haven't stopped to count the number of injured workers I have helped in the past 10 years, but the number is well more than 500 and closer to 1000.

For the past ten years I have always had at least one partner. In 2004 I decided go it alone. I have restricted my clientele to those with only the most serious injuries, however I am more than glad to consult with anyone who has had any work-related injury, and will never leave an injured worker "hanging" without advising him or her and perhaps referring him or her to other attorneys who practice in the area of workers compensation.

I hope you will enjoy this web site and learn more about workers compensation law in either the state of Kansas or Missouri. In both instances the law of workers compensation is "statutory law" - meaning the laws are promulgated by the respective legislatures of Kansas and Missouri. And I'm sorry to inform you that in too many instances the laws favor (in my humble opinion) the employer and not the employee; the insurance company and not the insured worker; big business and not the "little guy". If you would like some more information about how the laws are weak and how unfavorable the court decisions are, please read the writings I have placed on this site under the various headings. If you would like to do something about the problem of the lack of adequate legal protections for injured workers, then write or call your State Representative and Senator and tell them how you feel. Find out who your Missouri legislators are and find out who your Kansas legislators are.

You can bet your bottom dollar that the Chambers of Commerce, the Insurance lobby, Big Business, and other commercial interests are working hard to make sure that the Legislature does not do anything to improve the rights of injured workers.

Attorney Shea Stevens‘ practice concentrates exclusively on family law issues including: divorce, collaborative law, mediation, legal separation, paternity, custody, child support, maintenance, post divorce modifications, common law marriage, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements in both Kansas and Missouri. Ms. Stevens has experience in all aspects of family law, including contested custody issues, dividing high net worth cases and determining the value of one's business. Ms. Stevens has a team of professionals from accountants, financial advisors, realtors and therapists to provide clients the best possible service and outcome of their case.

Ms. Shea Stevens is a graduate of Kansas State University and University of Tulsa School of Law. She is actively involved in the local bar associations, including the Johnson County Family Law Inn of Court, Association of Women Lawyers, Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association and has given several CLE presentations on Ethics and Parenting Plans. Ms. Stevens has been recognized as a Superlawyer and Rising Star in Superlawyers (KS & MO), Top 50 female attorney in Kansas City, Top 100 attorney in Kansas City, Best of Johnson County - Johnson County Post and Best of the Bar - Family Law by the KC Business Journal.

When Shea is not in the office, she can be found outside. She is regularly on the sidelines cheering on her daughter, walking her dog, Polly, or possibly trying to get the golf ball to find its way into that annoying tiny hole.

attorneys.name: Timothy Stock Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Overland Park, KS
attorneys.bio:
Timothy Stock is a Senior Associate Attorney in the Overland Park, Kansas office who is committed to helping clients navigate challenging legal situations with confidence and care. He takes a client-centered approach that emphasizes clear explanations, thoughtful preparation, and steady guidance at every stage of the process. Timothy understands that these matters often affect families, finances, and futures, and he works to reduce uncertainty by keeping clients informed and supported as decisions are made.

Timothy earned his Juris Doctor from Washburn University School of Law. He also holds a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology with a minor in Philosophy and Sociology from Washburn University. This educational background supports his ability to understand client concerns, evaluate complex issues, and communicate effectively in high-stakes situations.

Before joining Stange Law Firm, Timothy developed a well-rounded professional background that includes several years of practicing domestic law in the Topeka area and service as a Public Defender with the Southeast Kansas Public Defender’s Office. He also brings significant experience managing complex technology projects for the Kansas Supreme Court, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Justice. These roles required strong coordination, risk management, and clear communication with multiple stakeholders, skills that carry over directly to his legal practice. Timothy applies this experience to manage cases efficiently, anticipate potential challenges, and remain focused on practical solutions for the individuals and families he represents.

attorneys.name: Jesse Tanksley
attorneys.practice_type: Negligence Lawyers in Hutchinson, KS
attorneys.bio:
With an original goal of becoming an FBI agent, Jesse Tanksley was inspired to become an attorney after gaining first-hand experience at a law firm during his time in law school.

The Hutchinson native graduated summa cum laude from Washburn University in 2006 with a Bachelor of Science, and he received a Juris Doctor from the University of Kansas School of Law in 2009. During law school, he was a note and comment editor for the University of Kansas Law Review, and he interned for the U.S. Attorney’s office in Kansas City, Kansas during his third year.

After graduating from law school and passing the bar exam, he began his career as a research attorney for the Kansas Court of Appeals, where he worked on a variety of criminal and civil appeals. After that, he worked for Stinson Leonard Street LLP in its Wichita office, where he primarily represented large companies in business and employment litigation.

Jesse joined Mann Wyatt & Tanksley in January 2015 and now focuses his practice on negligence and product liability cases.

He’s licensed to practice in Kansas state and federal court, as well as the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals. He’s a member of the Kansas Bar Association, the Reno County Bar Association, and the Kansas Trial Lawyers Association.

When not at work, Jesse can often be found at the soccer fields with his wife watching one of his four kids’ soccer games.

attorneys.name: H. Reed Walker
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Reed Walker, PA
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Overland Park, KS
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Walker has over 30 years of courtroom experience in family law and other civil litigation.

While ours is a general practice firm, we handle primarily civil litigation. We litigate, that is prepare and go to trial upon, if necessary, family law cases including divorce or dissolution of marriage; custody; child support; child visitation; guardian and conservatorships; wills, trusts, probate and estates.

Mr. Walker, our senior attorney, began practicing law in 1977. He graduated with Dean's Honors from Washburn University Law School in Topeka, Kansas. While a law student, he served on the Board of Editors of the Washburn Law Journal, and since graduation has served as an editor of state and local bar publications. He is currently a member of the Kansas Association for Justice and Kansas and Missouri Bar Associations. He has served as the president of the litigation section of the Kansas Bar Association; on the Board of Governors of the Kansas Trial Lawyers Association; and as president of the county bar association and chairman and current member of its grievance and ethics committee. He is a past president of the county bar foundation, the mission of which is charitable law-related, community-oriented causes. He is counsel of record in cases published by the Kansas appellate courts.

Mr. Walker is licensed to practice in the state (which includes municipal, district, and circuit) and federal courts of Kansas and Missouri; the federal 8th and 10th Circuit Courts of Appeal; and the United States Supreme Court. A significant portion of his time is spent litigating cases in court.

Other staff members, including paralegals and clerks (non-lawyers who are specially trained in the law and legal procedure), will talk with you, write you, answer questions, and help you understand the legal process, gather information and prepare cases for settlement or trial.

Achievements

In addition to successfully concluding thousands of family law cases in courts throughout the greater Kansas city area, we have collected well over one million dollars in personal injury settlements for our clients, and have written briefs for, and participated in, numerous appeals in the Kansas state and federal courts, as well as Writs of Certiorari to the United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Walker has achieved Martindale-Hubbell's highest peer review rating, "AV-Preeminent," which means judges and lawyers throughout the metro area know he meets very high criteria of general ethical standards, and has the highest ratings in his legal knowledge, analytical capabilities, judgment, communication ability, and legal experience. He is also a fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers, the purpose of which is to encourage the study, improve the practice, elevate the standards, and advance the cause of matrimonial law. He is listed in Who's Who in American Law and Who's Who in America.

He is among the top five percent of lawyers thus included in Missouri and Kansas Super Lawyers, and has received the Martindale-Hubbell Client Distinction Award for quality of service, overall value, responsiveness, and communication ability, as well as the Martindale-Hubbell 2021 Silver Client Champion Award. He is also a Master in the Johnson County Family Law Inns of Court and a member of the Johnson County Family Law Advisory Committee.

Goals

Our goal is to meet our clients' needs and exceed their expectations by being available to help them in times of crisis.

attorneys.name: Jerry Lee Wallentine
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Olathe, KS
attorneys.bio:
I began my career learning from some of the best, most experienced lawyers in Kansas and Missouri. That experience has helped me become a skilled trial lawyer. Now, as a private attorney, running my own law office for two decades, I advocate for clients in Johnson County, KS and the Kansas City, Missouri surrounding area. I have successfully advocated for many clients in the courtroom and out, in cases regarding serious injuries. I have helped hundreds of clients. When you are seriously injured, I help you get the money you deserve. I have experienced great success at jury trials, bench trials, and in settlement. Before I became an attorney, I was a persuasive professional speaker for 10 years. That experience greatly honed my skills to become a dynamic persuasive trial lawyer.

If you are dealing with a serious injury, you need skilled, dynamic, and aggressive representation by a quality trial lawyer. Wallentine Injury Law, LLC is one of the leading personal injury law firms in Kansas and Missouri. Our accomplished team of trial attorneys has the insight and expertise needed to handle even the most complex cases. We are dedicated to providing our clients with the best possible representation in court while striving for results-oriented outcomes that serve their interests.

Our injury lawyers understand how difficult it can be when you or a loved one has been injured due to someone else’s negligence. This is why we strive to provide our clients with knowledgeable legal guidance every step of the way—from filing paperwork and preparing for court appearances, all the way through the resolution of your case. We handle serious personal injury cases, including: deaths, bike accidents, pedestrian accidents, motor vehicle accidents, slip and fall accidents, dog bites, and defective products.

In a free initial, no obligation consultation, we can discuss the facts of your case and basic strategies. I utilize innovative, aggressive and dynamic defense strategies to protect my clients' rights and interests. I anticipate cases for trial rather than rushing to a settlement. This leads to better results whether your case goes to trial or does end up with a settlement. With my history as a professional public speaker, I utilize persuasive techniques for your benefit.

Our practice is based in Olathe, Kansas across the street from the Johnson County Courthouse. We are also in Kansas City, Missouri. Our attorneys and team of paralegals serve the citizens in the Kansas City area, inclu0ding Lenexa, Olathe, Shawnee, Overland Park, Mission Hills, Merriam, and all surrounding communities of Johnson County and Wyandotte County, as well as Jackson County, Missouri. Contact a zealous Kansas City lawyer who will fight for you! Call (913) 934-6333.

Matt joined Hovey Williams in 2007 after earning his law degree from the University of Missouri-Kansas City, where he graduated magna cum laude. Matt received his B.S. in Computer Science from the University of Missouri-Rolla, where he graduated summa cum laude.

attorneys.name: Michelle M. Watson
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Law Lawyers in Wichita, KS
attorneys.bio:
Michelle has a practice focusing on litigation defense, health care law, and business law.

She has extensive experience in medical malpractice defense for hospitals, hospices, clinics, physicians, dentists, and nurses. Michelle has also served a wide variety of clients in general insurance defense.

In Health Care Law, Michelle advises hospitals and physician clinics on issues such as HIPAA, HITECH, Stark, fraud and abuse and anti-kickback compliance. She also assists in patient security and care issues, policy and form compilation and review, and interacting with governmental agencies, as well as training and advice to healthcare ethics committees.

Michelle works with healthcare providers and business associates to conduct HIPAA and HITECH compliance audits and internal investigations. She has created a "HIPAA/HITECH Policy Manual" for Kansas providers and assists in implementation and training when the practice implements these new policies. She has assisted in several data breach responses, internal investigations and Office of Civil Rights compliance and investigation responses.

Michelle also represents business clients, including healthcare providers in contract reviews and disputes, assists in government investigations, and commercial litigation.

Born in Anchorage (AK) to a military family, Michelle has lived in six other states and in England before coming to Kansas and graduating cum laude from Washburn University School of Law in 1997. She received her undergraduate degree in Criminology from Florida State University.

Michelle is admitted to practice before the Supreme Court of Kansas, the United States District Court for Kansas, and the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals. She practiced in the appeals division of the Sedgwick County District Attorney's office before joining the former Boyer, Donaldson & Stewart firm which merged with Gilliland & Hayes, LLC in 2002. Michelle is a founding member of Gibson Watson Marino LLC.

She serves on the Wichita Bar Association's Civil Practice Committee and the Medical-Legal Committee, which she chaired 2003-2005. Ms. Watson was on the board, and vice president of legal affairs, for Kansas Health Ethics. She recently authored the Kansas chapter for the American Health Lawyers Association State Healthcare Privacy Laws Survey.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Mark A. Werner
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Pittsburg, KS
attorneys.bio:
Mark Werner is an attorney licensed to practice law in the State of Kansas, and before the U.S. District Court for the District of Kansas, as well as the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. Mark graduated from Kansas State University with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1979, and from the University of Kansas School of Law in 1982 with a Juris Doctor degree. Mark moved to Pittsburg in 1982, where he started his law practice, specializing in estate planning, business and commercial law, employment law, and insurance defense litigation, as well as a general civil and criminal practice.

In 1995, Mark joined City National Bank of Pittsburg (now Commerce Bank) as Vice President and Trust Officer and served as legal counsel to the Bank, and in 1999 took on the responsibilities of Vice President of Commercial Lending. In 2004, Mark was named the Pittsburg Market President of Citizens Bank, N. A Throughout his time in banking, Mark continued his private law practice part-time in the areas of estate planning and commercial law.

In 2011, Mark returned to the full-time practice of law, opening his own law firm. attorneys.name: Mit S. Winter
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Mission Woods, KS
attorneys.bio:
Mit Winter focuses his practice on helping businesses of all types and sizes navigate complex challenges, with considerable experience assisting companies in general commercial litigation and business disputes, class action litigation, intellectual property matters, and a broad array of collegiate sports matters.

Prior to joining Kennyhertz Perry, Mit worked for two different Am Law 100 firms in San Francisco and Kansas City, most recently as a shareholder in the commercial litigation group at Polsinelli. In that capacity, he represented a wide variety of clients in class action, intellectual property, and general business litigation matters and was identified by Missouri & Kansas Super Lawyers as a Rising Star in Business Litigation in 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, and 2018. Before moving to Kansas City and joining Polsinelli, Mit worked for Bingham McCutchen LLP where he represented clients such as Stanford University and Intel in class action and intellectual property litigation matters.

In addition to his commercial litigation practice, Mit has unique and broad experience assisting collegiate sports clients with their legal needs. At Polsinelli, Mit represented the Big 12 and Conference USA in numerous litigation matters and other matters arising from the governance of their respective members’ college sports programs. These matters included, among others, high profile challenges to the NCAA’s limit on the value of an athletic scholarship (O’Bannon v. NCAA, Alston v. NCAA), conference realignment matters, matters relating to conference broadcast agreements, assisting with objections to open records requests, Title IX issues, and concussion matters. At Bingham, Mit represented the NCAA in White v. NCAA and In re NCAA I-A Walk-on Football Players Litigation, challenges to NCAA rules on the value and number of athletic scholarships. As a result of this experience, Mit has dealt with many of the legal challenges that conferences and their member schools are faced with in administering and sponsoring high profile collegiate sports programs. In combination with his background as a Division I college basketball players, Mit is uniquely suited to assist collegiate sports clients with their legal issues.

attorneys.practice_type: Negligence Lawyers in Hutchinson, KS
attorneys.bio:
At a young age, Michael J. Wyatt admired the attorneys in movies who represented “the little guy.” He went on to receive his Bachelor of Arts (Summa Cum Laude) from Washburn University in 2004 and a Juris Doctor (with honors) from Washburn University School of Law in 2007. He then started his career with the Wichita defense firm of Klenda, Mitchell, Austerman & Zuercher, LLC.

Today, Mike is a partner at Mann Wyatt Tanksley Injury Attorneys Midwest Personal Injury Firm, a trial attorney, and an award-winning published author. He is passionate about helping clients in Kansas, Colorado, Missouri, and Oklahoma and has successfully settled and litigated many multi-million dollar cases.

Mike focuses his practice on the law of negligence, including wrongful death, automobile, and trucking accidents, catastrophic injury, home, and work explosions, products liability, nursing home neglect, and premises liability.

Mike is licensed in Kansas, Colorado, Missouri, and Oklahoma state and federal courts. He is a member of various bar associations, trial lawyer organizations, and has served on the executive board for the Kansas Trial Lawyer Association.

Mike has been named to the National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Trial Lawyers list numerous times as well as their Top 40 Under 40. He has also received the distinguished AVVO perfect rating for client communication, responsiveness, effectiveness, and value.

Mike has been named to the Rising Stars list published by Super Lawyers magazine and has been recognized by KC Magazine numerous times as one of Missouri and Kansas’ Top Attorneys and Outstanding Young Lawyers in personal injury law.

Mike enjoys the opportunity to serve in his local church and on the boards of several non-profit organizations. Mike’s most notable accomplishment is his longtime marriage to his wife, Jamie. He is the proud father of three children.

attorneys.name: Melinda G. Young
attorneys.practice_type: Car, truck & motorcyle wrecks Lawyers in Hutchinson, KS
attorneys.bio:
The best way to get to know me is to know why I am a lawyer. I did not grow up knowing I wanted to be a lawyer. There were no lawyers in my family, and I did not even know any lawyers. But, as my mother would tell you, two things have always driven me: standing up for anyone that has been hurt or treated unfairly, and the desire to correct an injustice in order to pave the way for a better future.

Once I discovered that as a lawyer, I could stand up for people that have been hurt and treated unfairly, I knew I had found my calling. I am proud to be a lawyer because I believe lawyers can level the playing field and ensure that everyone has a voice, not just those with power.

I was born and raised in Hutchinson, Kansas. After high school, I left Hutchinson and moved around a bit, searching for my passion in life. After several years, I realized that Kansas was my home and Kansans were who I wanted to help the most. I worked full-time for a law firm as a paralegal while attending college at night. I received my undergraduate degree from Friends University in Wichita, Kansas.

I received my law degree from Washburn University School of Law in Topeka, Kansas. During law school, I became an Editor for the Washburn Law Journal and a published author. I received the John F. Keuther Award for Outstanding Comment for my publication, Discrimination for the Sake of the Children.

After law school, I returned to Hutchinson and joined the law firm where I had previously worked as a paralegal. In 2013, I became a partner. In 2021, I formed my own firm in order to better serve those in my community.

When I am not working for my clients, I love spending time with my husband and daughter. You can usually find any one of us performing or participating in local theatre. My husband and daughter enjoy acting and singing. I, however, have the most fun performing improv, although I am not holding my breath waiting for Whose Line Is It Anyway? is call.

I am licensed in Kansas and by the United States District Courts in Kansas, Iowa, Oklahoma, Colorado, Illinois and Missouri. I am a member of the Kansas Trial Lawyers Association and Kansas Women Attorneys Association. I am currently handling injury cases including car, truck and motorcycle wrecks, pedestrian and bicycle injuries, falls and other injuries on another's property, inadequate security, nursing home, and wrongful termination.

attorneys.name: Coleman Younger
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Wichita, KS
attorneys.bio:
Coleman Younger is a passionate attorney who finds immense satisfaction in representing individuals against large insurance companies. He’s drawn to practicing personal injury because it is a meaningful way to help others during some of their most challenging times.

Coleman’s approach to his practice is rooted in client-focused efficiency. He believes in treating everyone with respect and friendliness, which helps to move cases along smoothly. For Coleman, setting clear expectations and maintaining open communication with clients is essential. He understands that clients are often scared and hurting after a traumatic event, and he makes it a priority to support them every step of the way.

Coleman is the lead attorney for our Wichita office.

Born and raised in Frankfort, Kansas, Coleman’s small-town upbringing instilled a strong sense of community in him. He attended Kansas State University, where he played roller hockey and captained the club team in his senior year. He then earned his law degree from Washburn University School of Law.

Outside of work, Coleman is an active member of the community, having coached youth flag football, served as a Rotary Club president, and volunteered at animal shelters. He also enjoys playing in hockey tournaments across the Midwest.
